Multiple cottages, houses, and cabins were also destroyed.
A couple of two-story hotel buildings sustained total destruction of their top floors and collapse of many walls on their first floors.

In Samburg, houses had roofs and exterior walls ripped off and mobile homes were destroyed. The city hall building, post office, a gas station, and several other buildings were damaged or destroyed.
Northeast of Samburg, the tornado began to weaken with the roof being blown off a farm building along Old Samburg Road.

Two more people were killed in Little Rock, Arkansas just after midnight.
In total, twelve people were killed on April 14–15 during a larger outbreak across the Southern United States.
Twenty-six fatalities occurred across North Carolina and Virginia on April 16.
An EF3 tornado near Hot Springs Village, Arkansas on April 25 caused significant damage and killed one person.
A long-track EF2 tornado in the Vilonia, Arkansas area on April 25 killed four people and injured 16 others.
From April 27 to early on the 28th, a series of devastating, long-tracked, violent tornadoes killed over 300 people throughout an area extending from Mississippi to Virginia.
One particularly devastating and long-lived EF5 wedge tornado tore across northern Alabama and into Tennessee, killing 72 people.
A large, long-tracked EF4 wedge tornado caused catastrophic damage in densely populated areas of Tuscaloosa and Birmingham, Alabama, killing 64 people.
319 tornado-related deaths occurred from April 27–28.
The total death toll from April 25–28 was 324 from 31 separate tornadoes.
Twenty-four additional fatalities occurred from separate thunderstorm impacts.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The first killer tornado of 1950 was a lone F3 tornado on January 13 which struck Polk County, Arkansas, killing one and injuring another.
An F4 tornado during a deadly outbreak left at least 18 people dead along an 82.6-mile-long track in Louisiana on February 12.
A deadly tornado outbreak between February 11–13 in the Southern United States produced eight killer tornadoes (six on February 12) that collectively left at least 45 people dead.
A long track F3 tornado in Louisiana tracked 74.5 miles and left five dead.
A long track F2 tornado in Louisiana traveled 58.4 miles and left another five dead.
At the end of March, 16 tornadoes in the Mississippi Valley resulted in one fatality.
A fatal F3 tornado in Tuckerman, Arkansas in early April killed one person.
A larger outbreak at the end of April in the Central Plains and Mississippi produced violent F4 tornadoes in Texas and Oklahoma, killing 11 people.
An outbreak across the Central Plains in early May resulted in one death.
Four tornadoes struck the United Kingdom at the end of May, killing four people.
An F3 tornado at the beginning of June north of Kosciusko, Mississippi killed two people.
A violent F4 tornado in June hit Southern McPherson, Kansas, killing one person.
A tornado outbreak in Wisconsin produced killer F2 and F4 tornadoes in Colby and Rhinelander respectively, which together killed three people.
The final major tornado event of the year in the United States, with four tornadoes striking Illinois and Arkansas, resulted in three deaths.
